Epicurean

ep-ih-kyoo-REE-uhn · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Epicurean is devoted to the pursuit of refined, sensory pleasure.

The couple's epicurean honeymoon consisted of nothing but tasting menus and rare vintages.

Worked Example

Their epicurean weekend consisted of a five-course tasting menu and a private wine cellar tour.

Epicurean describes a lifestyle devoted to refined pleasure, especially good food, wine, and comfort.

How Epicurean Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

extravagant

extravagant: spending or using resources lavishly

luxurious

luxurious: characterized by great comfort and extravagance

Antonyms

modest

modest: unpretentious in scale or amount

spartan

spartan: showing strict self-discipline and avoidance of comfort

How Strong Is It? — pampered → epicurean → excessive in every comfort

pampered vs. epicurean

pampered vs. epicurean: Being pampered is enjoying comfort provided by others; an epicurean actively seeks out refined pleasure as a way of life.

excessive in every comfort vs. epicurean

excessive in every comfort vs. epicurean: Taking comfort to an unhealthy extreme goes even further than simply living an epicurean lifestyle.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — Epicur

root — Epicur: Epicurus, an ancient Greek philosopher (Greek (proper name))

suffix — -ean

suffix — -ean: of or relating to (Greek/Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Epicur (the philosopher Epicurus) + -ean ("relating to") = relating to Epicurus's philosophy of pleasure.

Use the root in a new word: Epicureanism

Use the root in a new word: Epicureanism: The philosopher's full school of thought is called "Epicureanism" -- though ironically, Epicurus himself actually taught moderation, not excess.

Word Building

Word Choice

Epicurean comes from a real person's name (Epicurus), not a reusable root -- it's an eponym, much like how a word can be named after a person or place.
